evidence: A model result of the offline storm-water chain on the design years (A28R_301k_design_l15_snow_s934, years 10-19) and geography's 1.9 km depression tree, for PlaSim's hollows' store (climate/gcm/land_store.py). The store's curves sum phase 2b's hollows at common fills: every hollow holding the same share of its capacity, which spreads a cell's water over its hollows by their capacity, where phase 2b's pools fill by their own inflow; the cost of that lumping is measured offline (session-tools/agents/storm_water/stage_b_report.md). The floors are designs (a clay seal scaled from the HAPEX-Sahel plateau pools, sandy banks above a 1 m stage, a seal ten times tighter), the bowls' counts the terrain study's equilibrium law, their shape half Pike's fresh depth, and the routing shares phase 2a's routing under stand-in storms (Walnut Gulch's measured family and CM1's 6 km window over wet ground). The runoff tables read each 30-minute step as a storm of its own at a steady rate on soil the bucket's wetness gives, Green and Ampt at lunar gravity on designed surfaces, so a storm's memory from one step to the next is lost. No PlaSim run has used these tables.
reading_rule: Each cell is a T21 point j * nlon + i of PlaSim's grid (north to south from 0 E). Depths, areas and seepage are per unit of the grid's dryland area in the cell (dryland_km2), the basis of phase 2a's fates and phase 2b's per-cell results, which PlaSim carries over the whole T21 cell as it carries the bucket. store[age].capacity_m is the hollows' total volume (m of water); area_share and seepage_m_s (per floor) are the water area's share and the floors' seepage (m/s) with every hollow at the share grids.fill of its capacity, read between fills linearly in the square root of the fill (exact for the bowls) and nil at nil volume. shares[library][surface][age] split the slopes' runoff into the hollows, the rivers (the sea and the humid land), the ground below the roots (recharge) and the soil (the slopes' and channel beds' soak above the roots); they sum to 1. runoff_tables[surface][depth][wetness] is the share of a step's rain that runs off, bilinear in grids.rain_depth_mm (the step's rain on its wetted patch, mm in 30 minutes) and grids.wetness (the bucket's water over its 0.5 m capacity), held within both grids.
